u6_open.title: 1. U6: does pin 5 join VIN under the chip?
u6_open.instructions: Your annotation shows pin 4 unused, pin 5 reaching the upper end of R37 and the single pad of empty U6A, pin 3 reaching the PIR supply, pin 2 reaching C36, and pin 1 at GND. Only the hidden pin 5-to-pin 2 join remains in this batch. Numbers are package pins; grey labels give orientation only. The current R37-to-VIN connection is an older hypothesis, so it must not be used as proof of this join.

4.description: U6 pin 4 / L1: upper pad on the two-pad side

5.description: U6 pin 5 / L2: lower pad on the two-pad side

3.description: U6 pin 3 / R1: upper-right pad, candidate VOUT

2.description: U6 pin 2 / R2: middle-right pad, candidate VIN

1.description: U6 pin 1 / R3: lower-right pad, candidate GND

d6_open.title: 2. D6 beside PIC U4 and the programming connector J1
d6_open.instructions: Measure each D6 end against the three nearby connector nodes. The paths disappear near/under U4, so the photographs alone do not establish their destinations. Keep V and W as physical end names; do not assign diode pin numbers from these labels.

V.description: D6 upper metal end in this photo

W.description: D6 lower metal end, nearer J1

X.description: J1 pin 1 / VPP: rightmost square solder pad

Y.description: J1 pin 2 / VDD: second pad from the right
